scope: Proposition 4.10 (Finite simulations and endpoint predictors) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every bounded smooth empirical test of finitely many states on an admissible tree has the same limiting value as successively finer, finite smooth simulations from the corresponding endpoint states. For a single observation interval and a test with difference norm B/ √ n, the error is at most CT B √︁ log(1/h) + on(1). (4.28) The statement holds for replicated conditional tests, using the same predictor approximation on each copy. A linear query of bounded smooth outputs may be included after clipping; its spatial square tails are uniformly negligible in the successive approximation limits.
